pool.text: Belgrade became the seat of the Serbian king Stefan Dragutin.
Đurađ Branković returned Belgrade to the Hungarian king and made Smederevo his capital.
Noon bells in support of the Hungarian army have remained a church tradition.
Belgrade was conquered by the Ottomans and became the seat of the Sanjak.
Belgrade was once again named the capital of Serbia following the revolution.
A skull of a Paleolithic human was discovered on Cetinjska Street.
Belgrade opened its first airport.
The Pančevo Bridge crossing the Danube was opened.
The first Belgrade Grand Prix motor racing race was held.
The Luftwaffe heavily bombed the city after the Tripartite Pact signing.
Belgrade was bombed by the Allies during World War II.
Marshal Josip Broz Tito proclaimed the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia.
Construction of New Belgrade started.
The Nikola Tesla Museum was founded to preserve the inventor's personal items.
Coventry became twinned with Belgrade as part of international city relations.
Belgrade's first television station began broadcasting.
Belgrade hosted the first and founding conference of the Non-Aligned Movement.
Belgrade Nikola Tesla Airport was built.
A new museum foundation amassed thousands of art works from former Yugoslavia.
Belgrade faced the last major smallpox outbreak in Europe.
